backup.hint: Back up everything this browser stores for the connected radio — message history, discovered nodes, automation rules, preferences, and channel metadata — into a single file encrypted with a passphrase you choose. The file restores on any machine, even one that has never seen this radio.
backup.secretsExcluded: Your LLM API key is never included in a backup. It stays in its own encrypted store on this device.
backup.exportIntro: Choose a passphrase to encrypt the backup. It is never stored — not in the file, not on this device — so if you forget it the backup cannot be opened by anyone, including you.
backup.passphraseHint: Use a long, unique passphrase. It is the only thing protecting the file.
backup.passphraseMismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
backup.includeIdentityWarning: Adds the radio's identity so you can restore this node — same public key, same routes — onto replacement hardware. Anyone who obtains this file AND its passphrase can impersonate your node on the mesh. Store it accordingly.
backup.importIntro: Pick a backup file and enter its passphrase. You will see exactly what changes before anything is written.
backup.importDoneIdentity: Backup restored — reboot the radio to finish switching identity
backup.importUnsaved: Backup restored to this session only — it could not be saved to this browser, so reloading will lose it
backup.importUnsavedIdentity: Identity replaced — reboot the radio to finish. The restored data could not be saved to this browser, so reloading will lose it
backup.previewAdvertsEvicted: Cache is full — {{count}} of the oldest cached nodes are dropped to make room
backup.sessionChanged: the radio session changed before this could finish — reconnect and try again
backup.mismatchWarning: This backup is from a different radio (…{{backup}}) than the one connected (…{{connected}}). Restoring it grafts another node's message history, discovered nodes, automation rules and preferences onto this one — and a restored preference can arm the restored rules, which then act on this radio.
backup.restoreIdentityWarning: This overwrites the connected radio's private key with the one in the backup. Its current identity is destroyed and cannot be recovered unless you have a backup of it. The radio must be rebooted afterwards, and contacts that knew its old public key will no longer reach it. Anyone else holding this file AND its passphrase can put the same identity on their own hardware and impersonate the node on the mesh.
backup.restoreIdentityConfirm: This cannot be undone. Type {{node}} to confirm you are replacing this radio's identity.

identityError.rejected: The radio rejected the key in this backup as invalid.

readError.notABackup: That file is not a MeshCore backup.

recovery.hint: This radio's identity exists only in its own flash. Regenerate it under a recovery phrase so you can put the same identity onto replacement hardware if the radio is ever lost.
recovery.title: Create a recovery phrase
recovery.explainIntro: The identity this radio holds was generated inside it, and it can never be given a recovery phrase after the fact. The only way to get a recoverable identity is to replace this one with a new identity generated from a phrase.
recovery.costPubkey: Your public key changes. Every contact has to add you again, and messages from peers who still hold your old key will not reach you.
recovery.costOld: The current identity is erased from the radio. Unless you back it up first, it is gone for good.
recovery.costSecrets: A remembered AI key and saved repeater passwords belong to the old identity and will need entering again.
recovery.costKept: Message history, discovered nodes, automation rules and preferences in this browser carry over to the new identity.
recovery.backupFirst: Back up the current identity first
recovery.phraseIntro: Write these {{count}} words down on paper, in order. They are the only way to restore the new identity.
recovery.phraseWarning: Anyone who sees this phrase can put your identity on their own radio and impersonate you on the mesh. Never type it into a website, photograph it, or keep it in a cloud note.
recovery.phraseWritten: I have written the phrase down
recovery.confirmIntro: Enter the words at these positions from your written copy. A phrase that was never written down is worse than none, because it feels like a backup.
recovery.confirmWrong: One or more words do not match. Check your written copy, or go back to see the phrase again.
recovery.passphraseIntro: Choose a passphrase to lock this device's record of the new identity, its identity vault. You will need it to manage this identity later. It does not protect the phrase on paper.
recovery.passphraseHint: Use a long, unique passphrase. Without it, this device cannot open the vault.
recovery.remember: Remember the phrase on this device
recovery.rememberWarning: Off unless you need it. When on, the phrase is kept inside the vault, so anyone with this browser profile and the passphrase can read it back and take over every identity it makes.
recovery.writeIntro: The radio's current identity will be replaced by the one your phrase derives. Its public key will be:
recovery.writeReboot: The radio then reboots, and this app reconnects and checks that it reports exactly this public key.
recovery.rebooting: Identity written — rebooting the radio to verify it

error.unsupported: This radio's firmware does not support replacing its identity.
error.rejected: The radio refused the new key as invalid, so it kept its current identity. A generated phrase should never be refused: do not rely on this phrase, and please report this.
error.writeFailed: The radio could not save the new identity to its flash, so it kept its current one. Reboot the radio and try again; if it keeps failing, its storage may be full.
error.vault: The identity vault could not be saved on this device ({{error}}). Nothing was written to the radio.
error.unconfirmed: The radio did not confirm the write, so it may or may not hold the new identity. It is being rebooted to find out, and this app compares its public key when it reconnects. Keep your written phrase until then.
error.unsaved: This browser's data could not be saved under the new identity. Reloading before the radio reconnects will lose it.
error.rebootFailed: The radio did not reboot ({{error}}). Reboot it yourself without reloading this page; this app checks its public key when it reconnects.
error.generate: A recovery phrase could not be generated ({{error}}).

recovery.checkOk: Verified. The radio reports public key {{pubkey}}, exactly the one your recovery phrase derives. The phrase on paper restores this identity.
recovery.checkReadd: Your contacts still know your old public key. Send a flood advert so the mesh hears the new one, and ask your contacts to add you again.
recovery.checkMismatch: Verification failed. The radio reports public key {{actual}}, but your recovery phrase derives {{expected}}. The phrase on paper does not restore the identity on this radio. Do not rely on it, and please report this.
recovery.checkNotLanded: The write never reached the radio: it still reports its previous public key {{pubkey}}, so its identity is unchanged. The phrase you wrote down was never installed. Destroy it, and run the wizard again to create a new one.

restore.title: Restore from a recovery phrase
restore.enterIntro: Type the recovery phrase you wrote down, in order, with a space between words. It is checked on this device and never leaves it.
restore.unknownWord: Word {{n}}, “{{word}}”, is not in the recovery word list.

phraseError.wordCount: A recovery phrase has 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24 words. Check for a missing or extra word.
phraseError.unknownWord: Word {{n}} is not in the recovery word list.
phraseError.checksum: Every word is valid, but the phrase does not add up: a word is wrong or out of order. Check it against your written copy. A phrase that fails here would restore a different identity, so it is never used.
phraseError.reservedKey: This phrase derives a key MeshCore radios refuse, so it cannot be one this app generated. Check it against your written copy.

restore.previewIntro: This phrase restores the identity with public key:
restore.previewCheck: Compare it with the public key your contacts know you by. If it is not the one you expected, go back and check the phrase: nothing has been written yet.
restore.vaultKnown: This device has an identity vault for this phrase.
restore.vaultUnknown: This device has no identity vault for this phrase yet. One is created for it as part of the restore.
restore.alreadyHeld: The connected radio already holds this identity, so nothing is written to it. You can still record it in this device's identity vault.
restore.historyNote: The phrase restores the identity, not its messages. This browser may still hold history for this identity, but it only opens on a radio with the same channels as the one that wrote it; otherwise it is replaced once this radio starts saving. A backup file is what carries history to another radio or browser.
restore.replaceErase: The radio's current identity is erased. Unless you back it up first, it is gone for good.
restore.replaceContacts: Anyone who added this radio as it is now will no longer reach it. Contacts of the restored identity will reach you again.
restore.unlockIntro: Enter the passphrase of this device's identity vault for this phrase, so the restored identity is recorded in it.
restore.replaceVault: I do not know this passphrase — replace the vault
restore.replaceVaultHint: The vault is deleted and a new one created under a new passphrase. The phrase itself restores everything that matters; only the names of any other identities it lists here are lost.
restore.replaceVaultIntro: Choose a passphrase for the new identity vault that replaces the old one on this device.
restore.passphraseIntro: Choose a passphrase to lock this device's record of the restored identity, its identity vault. You will need it to manage this identity later. It does not protect the phrase on paper.

vaultError.notFound: This device's vault for the phrase has gone, perhaps deleted in another tab. Go back to the phrase and continue again.
vaultError.exists: A vault for this phrase appeared on this device while you were working, perhaps from another tab. Go back to the phrase and continue again.
vaultError.unsupportedVersion: This device's vault for the phrase was written by a newer version of this app, which is needed to open it.
vaultError.corrupt: The passphrase is right, but this device's vault for the phrase is damaged. Replace the vault to continue.
vaultError.stale: The vault was changed in another tab. Go back to the phrase and continue again.

error.vault: The identity vault could not be saved on this device ({{error}}). Nothing was written to the radio.
error.derive: The phrase could not be checked ({{error}}).
error.unconfirmed: The radio did not confirm the write, so it may or may not hold the restored identity. It is being rebooted to find out, and this app compares its public key when it reconnects.

restore.saved: Identity recorded in this device's vault
restore.rebooting: Identity restored — rebooting the radio to verify it
restore.checkOk: Verified. The radio reports public key {{pubkey}}, exactly the one your recovery phrase derives. Your identity is restored.
restore.checkReadd: Contacts who knew this identity can reach you again. Send a flood advert so the mesh learns where it is now.
restore.checkNotLanded: The write never reached the radio: it still reports its previous public key {{pubkey}}, so its identity is unchanged. Your phrase is fine; run the restore again.
restore.checkMismatch: Verification failed. The radio reports public key {{actual}}, but your recovery phrase derives {{expected}}. The restore did not take: keep your written phrase, and please report this.
restore.offerBody: This browser has not seen this radio before. If it replaces one you lost, you can put your old identity back onto it from your recovery phrase.
restore.offerLater: You can also do this later from Settings, under Identity.

persona.title: Personas
persona.lockedHint: Unlock a recovery phrase's vault to see the personas it has made and switch between them.
persona.liveNotListed: The radio's current identity is not one of this phrase's personas, so there is nowhere to keep its name, channels and contacts. Switch to one of these from a radio that holds one of them, or restore one from the phrase first.
persona.newIntro: A new persona is a separate identity made from the same phrase. It starts with its own name, no location, only the Public channel and no contacts, so nothing ties it to the others.
persona.switchIntro: This puts the persona's key on the radio and gives it back the radio-side state it had when it was last live. It can take up to a minute with a full contact list.
persona.switchRadio: The radio's name, location, channels and contacts are replaced with this persona's. The current persona's are kept on this device for when you switch back.
persona.switchBrowser: Message history, discovered nodes, preferences and automation rules in this browser switch to this persona's own.
persona.switchContacts: Peers know each persona by its own key. Contacts reach this persona only if they added it.
persona.heardElsewhere: {{name}} has been heard on the mesh during this session, so another radio is running it. Two radios with one identity break message delivery and acknowledgements for both. Switch only if that radio has stopped using it.
persona.heardElsewhereAck: The other radio no longer uses this identity
persona.announce: Announce the persona to the whole mesh when done

stage.importing: Writing the new key to the radio…

verbs.help: Shows this list, filtered to the commands whose syntax contains the text you pass.
verbs.ver: Reports the firmware version the node is running.
verbs.board: Reports the hardware the firmware was built for.
verbs.clock: Reports the node's current time, in UTC.
verbs.clockSync: Sets the node's clock from this computer's.
verbs.time: Sets the node's clock to a specific Unix epoch time.
verbs.advert: Sends one advert across the whole mesh. Everyone who hears it pays airtime for it.
verbs.advertZeroHop: Sends one advert to direct neighbors only, so it is never repeated.
verbs.neighbors: Lists the eight nodes this repeater heard advertise most recently.
verbs.neighborRemove: Forgets every neighbor whose public key starts with the given prefix. A bare space matches all of them.
verbs.discoverNeighbors: Asks direct neighbors to identify themselves.
verbs.clearStats: Resets the node's packet and airtime counters to zero.
verbs.logStart: Begins capturing a receive log to the node's storage.
verbs.logErase: Deletes the captured receive log from the node's storage.
verbs.getRole: Reports whether the node is a repeater, room server or sensor.
verbs.getOwnerInfo: Reports the free-text owner information the node carries.
verbs.setOwnerInfo: Sets the free-text owner information. A “|” starts a new line.
verbs.password: Changes the admin password, and admits anyone already using it to the admin list.
verbs.powersaving: Reports or sets whether the node sleeps between transmissions.
verbs.setperm: Grants a companion guest (0), read-only (1), read-write (2) or admin (3) access. Omit the level to revoke it.
verbs.startOta: Puts the node into over-the-air firmware update mode.
verbs.reboot: Restarts the node. It answers nothing and is unreachable until it comes back.
verbs.poweroff: Shuts the node down. It stays off until someone power-cycles it in person.
verbs.erase: Factory-resets the node, wiping its identity and every setting. The firmware accepts this over serial only.

config.intro: Values are read from the node on demand, one command at a time, so the tab doesn't spend this repeater's airtime unless you ask it to. Load a card to see its current settings — a field that never answers can be retried on its own.

name.label: Name
name.hint: The name this node advertises to the mesh.

radio.label: Radio
radio.hint: Frequency, bandwidth, spreading factor and coding rate. Every node that should hear this one must match them exactly.

tx.label: TX Power
tx.hint: Transmit power. Higher reaches further and costs more battery; it does not help if the other end can't reply.

gps.label: GPS module
gps.hint: Powers the on-board GPS receiver, on boards that have one.

gpsAdvert.label: Advertised location
gpsAdvert.hint: Whether adverts carry the live GPS fix, the fixed coordinates above, or no location at all.

repeat.label: Repeat
repeat.hint: Whether this node forwards other nodes' packets. Turn it off to make the node a leaf that only speaks for itself.

floodAdvertInterval.label: Flood advert interval
floodAdvertInterval.hint: How often this node floods an advert across the whole mesh. Floods reach everyone and cost everyone airtime, so longer is kinder.

advertInterval.label: Zero-hop advert interval
advertInterval.hint: How often this node advertises to direct neighbors only. Cheap, because it is never repeated.

floodMax.label: Max flood hops
floodMax.hint: How many hops a flood may already have taken and still be repeated by this node. 0 stops it forwarding floods at all.

txdelay.label: Flood TX delay factor
txdelay.hint: Scales the random wait before repeating a flood, which keeps neighbors that heard the same packet from transmitting over each other. Multiplied by the packet's airtime, so it isn't a fixed duration. 0 removes the wait.

directTxdelay.label: Direct TX delay factor
directTxdelay.hint: The same collision-avoidance factor, applied to packets on a known route rather than a flood. Lower, because fewer nodes compete to repeat them.

dutycycle.label: Duty cycle
dutycycle.hint: Share of the time this node is allowed to transmit. Some regions cap this by law.

loopDetect.label: Loop detection
loopDetect.hint: How aggressively repeated packets that have already passed through here are suppressed. Stricter saves airtime and risks dropping a legitimate retransmission.

pathHashMode.label: Advert path hash size
pathHashMode.hint: Bytes used to identify each hop in this node's own adverts. More bytes make collisions between similar nodes less likely and make those adverts slightly larger. Forwarding is unaffected.

multiAcks.label: Multi-acks
multiAcks.hint: Lets several acknowledgments ride in one packet instead of one each.

cad.label: Hardware CAD
cad.hint: Uses the radio's channel-activity detection to wait for a quiet channel before transmitting.

radioFemRxgain.label: FEM RX gain
